text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I want to run a validation campaign for a new driver+firmware+kernel combo to try to reduce the GPU resets / Xid noise we've seen. Proposing a canary batch of 10 nodes in us-west2 (low-traffic ASG) tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Thoughts?

priya: +1 on canary. Can we publish a short checklist of what the canary will run and which metrics we watch? Also what rollback criteria.

ajex: typo :), alex: Will do — draft checklist below. Main goals: reduce Xid spikes (esp Xid 13/31/43), cut ECC SBE trend, and avoid p95 latency regressions for inference.

alex: Checklist (smoke + telemetry):
```
1) node snapshot: `kubectl get nodes -l canary=true -o wide` and save `nvidia-smi -q` output
2) install driver version: dpkg/rpm or our imaging tool (image v2026-05-driver-520.61)
3) firmware flash step (if needed) — run `fwupdater --apply <fw.bin>` with dry-run first
4) boot into kernel 6.1.27-rc (test kernel image) and ensure `nvidia.ko` autoloads
5) run stress job: `python3 infra/qa/gpu_stress.py --iters 300 --seq 1024 --batch 8`
6) collect metrics for 6h: `gpu.xid.count`, `gpu.reset.count`, `gpu.ecc.sbe`, `gpu.util` and p95/p99 latency on a representative route
7) post-mortem checks: dmesg, /var/log/messages, `journalctl -k | grep NVRM` and `dmesg | tail -n 200`
```

jordan: Add a quick smoke inference: `scripts/smoke_infer.sh --model llama-7b --tokens 256` to confirm no silent hangs. Also run the stress job in a loop with small gaps to surface thermal/driver leak issues.

morgan: Drain/replace policy? If a canary node shows >=5 Xid events OR any hard GPU reset (reset count >0) within the 6h window, do we auto-drain it and mark for hardware diag? I worry about noisy PID-level retries.

priya: Proposed thresholds:
- Xid event threshold: 3+ in 6 hours for canary -> mark for manual review
- GPU reset: any non-zero reset count -> drain node
- ECC SBE: sustained >10 SBE/day -> schedule hardware replacement
- Latency: p95 > baseline * 1.15 OR error rate >0.5% -> rollback

alex: Agreed. For canary we should be conservative: manual gate for 3+ Xids, automatic drain on reset. If canary fails, we stop rollout and collect full traces.

priya: Example dmesg patterns we should watch (from last incident):
```
May 10 01:12:09 host kernel: NVRM: Xid (13): PID 4623 0x00000004 0x00000000
May 10 01:12:09 host kernel: NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 10 01:12:12 host kernel: nvidia: GPU reset count: 1
```

alex: Also ensure telemetry correlation: we need to correlate `gpu.xid.count` spikes with `node.disk.io`, `node.net.errors` and kernel OOMs. Past pattern showed Xid spikes aligned with noisy compute-IO jobs.

jordan: Quick commands I use for post-checks:
```
# check driver and modules
modinfo nvidia | egrep "version|filename"
# gpu details
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv
# look for NVRM entries
journalctl -k --since "6 hours ago" | grep -i NVRM
```

morgan: We should also run a small kernel module stress test: repeatedly load/unload `nvidia` 50 times and watch for leaks: `for i in $(seq 50); do rmmod nvidia && modprobe nvidia; sleep 2; done` (run in maintenance window).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary-run scheduled by alex at 1805127200 (job id: canary-2026-05-xx-01). Will post status updates to this thread.

alex: Ownership: I'll own the overall plan + rollback. @jordan you're on telemetry collection and stress harness. @priya you're on validation checks and gating. @morgan you'll own the drain/replace playbook for failing nodes?

jordan: yep, I'll wire the metrics and dashboards for quick review. Will add panels for `gpu.xid.count` per GPU, `gpu.reset.count` and latency heatmap for the canary pool.

priya: For rollout cadence, do 10 nodes -> hold for 6h -> if green, 30% -> hold 12h -> full roll by 48h. We should keep a rollback window open during each hold.

morgan: Cost/impact note: run heavy stress between 02:00-06:00 UTC to avoid peak. We'll limit canary ASG to non-prod tenants only. Also set `autoscaler.min=0` on canary nodegroup to avoid spilling traffic.

alex: Rollback criteria restated for the rollout automation:
- Any canary node with GPU reset >0 -> immediate rollback of that node's image and drain
- Canary cohort averaged Xid rate > baseline+200% -> stop and rollback cohort
- p95 latency regression > 15% OR error rate increase > 0.5% -> stop and rollback

priya: Small ask: add a short runbook snippet to detect false positives (e.g., misreported resets due to kernel module version mismatch). Example: `modinfo nvidia | grep -i version` must match driver package. If mismatch, mark as imaging issue not hardware.

alex: Final actions:
- jordan: add dashboards and alert rules (ETA: today EOD)
- priya: prepare validation checklist doc and runbook (ETA: today EOD)
- morgan: prepare drain/replace infra and a small hardware diag checklist (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- alex: kick canary at 02:00 UTC tomorrow if all green, will post job id here

priya: :thumbsup: Approving. Please tag me in the final canary job message.

jordan: I'll also snapshot one canary node with `sosreport` before changes so we have a clean forensic baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary job canary-2026-05-xx-01 started (step 1 image push). Progress updates will follow.

alex: Thanks all — will post results in this thread. If you see anything odd ping @oncall.

morgan: I'll be on standby during the 02:00 run. :coffee:
